title: Can a mid-predator be made to hunt — a badger that takes small prey and vermin without becoming a general large predator? REBUILD of E32, which was vacuous: assignFromMatrix gave BADGER seasons 2,3 and the replicate runs in season 0, so applyLive zeroed the badger entry and NOT ONE BADGER reached the map in either arm (badgers 0/0 across every sample). The subject of the experiment was held out of season by the tool's own roster — the same way E21's criterion turned out vacuous (addendum 51). This rebuild forces BADGER onto all four seasons AFTER assignFromMatrix, using the key the POOL reports (keyFor('land', token) returns the BARE TOKEN, so an assumed 'land:BADGER' is a phantom the roster writes and applyLive never reads — that mistake made E32b's first run as vacuous as E32's), and verifies by reading the badger entry's quantity back AFTER applyLive and asserts a badger is actually present before the arms are compared. One arm flips LARGE_PREDATOR on the badger's castes, which also makes the tool's ecology switch arm it; the control leaves the badger BENIGN as shipped. The fork is not whether the badger hunts but WHAT it attacks.
fork: Does arming a mid-predator make it hunt small prey only, or anything it meets — and does the LARGE_PREDATOR flag also move it into DF's scarcer large-predator spawn pool.

predictions.expects: badgers are present in both arms; the armed badger kills small prey and vermin (groundhog, skunk, porcupine, rats) and never a citizen, a fort animal, or anything above its own weight

predictions.model: the flag makes a general predator
predictions.expects: badgers present in both arms; the armed badger attacks whatever it meets, including large animals and the fort's own, so the class needs a SIZE FILTER on the relation targets rather than just the caste flag

predictions.model: the flag moves the species into DF's large-predator pool
predictions.expects: badgers arrive in the CONTROL arm but not in the armed one — the wiki's rule is that a biome supports about seven large-predator species chosen by a d100 under FREQUENCY, and a badger at frequency 5 would rarely win a slot, so arming a mid-predator would make it RARER rather than fiercer and the class cannot be built on the flag at all

predictions.model: the badger is armed but never meets anything
predictions.expects: badgers present, zero attacks in both arms; the coupling needs prey written within the nudge radius rather than left to chance

kill_criterion: with badgers actually on the map, the armed badger taking small prey and vermin and nothing else, 2 of 2, ships a mid-predator class; a badger taking anything it meets means the class needs a SIZE FILTER on the relation targets rather than just the flag; badgers still absent means the flag itself moved the species into the large-predator pool and a mid-predator class cannot be built on it at all
culling: drop a replicate on any changed save
a replicate in which NO badger ever appears is reported as a trigger failure, not as evidence the badger does not hunt

arms.name: armed
pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.layers.land=true; cfg.layers.water=false; cfg.layers.cavern=false; local f=0; for _,cr in ipairs(df.global.world.raws.creatures.all) do if cr.creature_id=='BADGER' then for _,c in ipairs(cr.caste) do c.flags.LARGE_PREDATOR=true; f=f+1 end end end; local pool=sw.buildPool(cfg); local n=0; for _,e in ipairs(pool) do if e.inEmbark and sw.defaultAllow(e) then cfg.allow[e.key]=true; n=n+1 end end; local a=sw.assignFromMatrix(cfg,pool); cfg.groups.enabled=true; cfg.groups.coupling=true; cfg.groups.pack=4; cfg.ecology.enabled=true; local bk=nil; for _,e in ipairs(pool) do if e.token=='BADGER' and e.layer=='land' then bk=e.key end end; if bk then sw.setAssign(cfg,bk,{0,1,2,3}); cfg.allow[bk]=true end; print(('e32b: BADGER pool key=%s seasons now %s'):format(tostring(bk), bk and table.concat(cfg.assign[bk] or {},',') or 'NO POOL ENTRY')); sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.applyLive(cfg, df.global.cur_season); sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.enableSched(); print(('e32: %d badger castes flipped — BADGER castes flipped to LARGE_PREDATOR; %d allowed, %d assigned, ecology on'):format(f,n,a))

local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local rs=sw.getEmbarkRegions(); local q,cnt=0,0; for _,pop in ipairs(df.global.world.populations.all) do local c=df.creature_raw.find(pop.race); if c and c.creature_id=='BADGER' and sw.managedPop(pop,rs,{land=true}) then q=q+pop.quantity; cnt=cnt+1 end end; print(('e32b: VERIFY %d badger entries managed, total quantity after applyLive = %d (zero here means the '..'badger is still excluded and the replicate is vacuous)'):format(cnt,q))

local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local by=sw.WILD.countByLayer(); local badger,armed=0,0; for _,cr in ipairs(df.global.world.raws.creatures.all) do if cr.creature_id=='BADGER' then for _,c in ipairs(cr.caste) do if c.flags.LARGE_PREDATOR then armed=armed+1 end end end end; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if not dfhack.units.isDead(u) then local c=df.creature_raw.find(u.race); if c and c.creature_id=='BADGER' then badger=badger+1 end end end; local cz=0; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isCitizen(u) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) then cz=cz+1 end end; print(('e32b: land=%d badgers=%d armed_castes=%d citizens=%d day=%d'):format(by.land,badger,armed,cz,math.floor(df.global.cur_year_tick/1200)))
